utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Good morning especially, Mr. Vukovic. May we remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning, which is still applicable. Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Petrovic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Vukovic. During the break yesterday afternoon and evening, did you perhaps remember the building where your mother lives?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even try to think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P172, the one on which he started marking something yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 10, or rather, the map of insula number 10. I don't know if it's on the ELMO properly, because I can't see it on my own monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can it please be zoomed out a bit, because we can't see it properly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you please mark for us the house where you say your mother lives. Could you please show it on this map, and could you please shade that particular building, if that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document also be admitted into evidence? My colleague kindly provided the same map of insula number 10 which does not have any markings on it, so we have P172, on the one hand, and on the other hand, the drawing that I am tendering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be marked D79.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness please be shown document P63, tab 9. Your Honour, since this is a very voluminous document, I photocopied the pages that are important for us here from that particular document so that our work would be facilitated as much as possible. So could it please be distributed to everyone, yourself included. So this is P63, tab 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are pages 1100 -- 1190745. That's one. The other one is 90 -- 01190750, and also the translation into B/C/S. All of this from tab 9 of this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, on page 1 of this document -- please look at the first page of this document. Please be so kind as to put it on the overhead projector. It's going to make things easier. Would you please be so kind as to put a circle around building number 4, the one that is marked on this map.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the next page of the document and then tell us: Is this the building that is at Buniceva Poljana number 6? In order to assist you, the document in question is a document of the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments. Mr. Vetma and Mr. Franic are the authors of this document and it has to do with the damage sustained by buildings in the Old Town in the period from 1991 to 1992. So can you see Buniceva Poljana number 6 here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this building here, and it's also half of this building which can be seen in the background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The record should reveal that the witness identified neither of the buildings in the foreground on the left and in the right half of the photograph, but a building somewhat in the background between the two, which is in the second quarter from the left of the photograph. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the building at Buniceva Poljana number 6 is what can be seen on this photograph on page 2; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, please look at page 3 in B/C/S. The translation is here. Before we move on to that, could you please be so kind as to answer the following question: The house where your mother lives, was it hit on the roof?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be so kind as to tell us, since I showed you the building in Buniceva Poljana number 4, I showed you the building at Buniceva Poljana number 6, and you showed and marked here for us a few minutes ago yet another building altogether as the building where your mother lives. When looking at the map of the town of Dubrovnik, do you know how to mark where your mother's home is?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I don't understand your question. Could you please repeat it for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is as follows: On the map of the town of Dubrovnik, do you know how to mark the place where your mother lives?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already done that on the other diagram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you told us yesterday that your mother lives at Buniceva Poljana 4 or Buniceva Poljana 6, I presented to you yesterday report 10-3, which pertains to Buniceva Poljana number 4, and I now showed you a document where Buniceva Poljana number 6 can be seen, and at the beginning of the morning session, you marked a completely different building for us. My question is: Do you know at all, on the map of the town of Dubrovnik, or rather, the Old Town, how to mark where your mother lives?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to make things clearer to you, Mr. Petrovic, I'm just going to give a brief answer. My statement, namely 4 or 6, does not diminish the importance of my lack of security in terms of the number itself. I was not sure whether it was 4 or 6 or something else. So this number is totally irrelevant. However, what is quite unequivocal and what I can confirm most definitely is that what I marked - excuse me - what I marked with the little dots is definitely my mother's house. I'm just asking you whether you are sure enough as to what you're talking about, and are you familiar with the situation in Buniceva Poljana?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document, which is an extract from P63/9, where the witness marked the building of Buniceva Poljana number 6, could it please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just add something to this? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Mr. Vukovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, in order to make things clearer, Buniceva Poljana is irregularly shaped. Its structure of buildings and entrances to buildings are not customary in terms of what a square usually looks like and what the entrances into the buildings are. The buildings are entered into from small approaches leading to the square, although even these little approaches are called Buniceva Poljana. And the entrance is underneath this, and I can tell you exactly where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can the exhibit please be admitted into evidence, or rather, the document that I proposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, the document is already in evidence, and this extract hasn't been specifically marked, so I don't really see that we need it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the first page of this document was marked by the witness. He put a circle around Buniceva Poljana number 6, and he did that on the ELMO. And that is why I would like to have this admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Can I just say something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute. I had overlooked that, Mr. Petrovic. Thank you. It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The drawing is D80.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I -- just for a moment. Mr. Vukovic -- my learned friend Mr. Petrovic I think stopped him just before he was trying to complete an answer, and he indicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He was completing a further statement. I've allowed him one opportunity to do that, and I think, Mr. Re, if you want to take it up, you can in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I withdraw this. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, you said that from some friends or colleagues of yours, you learned that allegedly the damage sustained by the Old Town was 17 million US dollars. Is that what you told us here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 17.5 million US dollars. That was on the basis of the preliminary report. However, there was another figure that was bandied about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just asking you if that was what you said yesterday, or rather, the day before yesterday before the Court. If that is what you said, that will suffice and I don't ask you anything else. In the document that was admitted before this Honourable Trial Chamber and which is in tab P63, or rather, in Prosecution Exhibit P63, tab 9 -- and could that document please be given to the witness. This is a document which is an estimate given by the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments. This document was compiled by Vetma and Franic. The total estimate of the damage for 1991 and 1992, Mr. Vukovic, is around 5.200.000 dollars. Could you please be so kind as to tell us how come it is possible that Vetma and Franic gave an estimate of 5.2 million and that your estimate is --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [In English] That's tab 6, and we now need tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. The witness -- it's not the witness's estimate. Mr. Vukovic's evidence was what he heard. It is not his own estimate. The way it's been presented to him is as if it is his own estimate which he has come to himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's right, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to rephrase my question, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were informed that the damage was 17.5 million dollars. If I tell you that Vetma and Franic placed the total damage for the entire period of 1991 and 1992 at 5.2 million, please tell me: Which one of these two estimates do you believe more?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, for your own information, I have to say that what you received from me was unofficial information. It was received, if I can put it that way, an institution that has to do with reconstruction in an operative fashion. So there were two versions that they made. One was based on what our estimate was, the one that we had done, and the other one was amended, or supplemented, because at that moment not all the indirect damage was taken into account in terms of the damage due to detonations and vibrations, and those that caused such destruction. So I really cannot make any further comment with regard to this particular piece of information, because actually all three documents show that the material that we worked on meant that it had to be improved all the time, and it indicated that the damage was certainly not at the levels that were initially established. This figure of 17.5 million dollars, I cannot tell you when it was established, whether it was established before what my colleagues Mr. Franic and Mr. Vetma did or after that. So if we understand this to be a process that went on and that in a way was being amended and supplemented, then I think that we can believe all three pieces of information, but this process of supplementing information actually went on from the moment when my colleagues Mr. Franic and Mr. Vetma started with the figure of 5.2 million, and then it moved on to 17.5 million, and 54 million ultimately. I'm telling you that all of this is unofficial because I did not take part in it myself. I cannot give you an exact figure, but I can tell you that I believe all three elements.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P63, tab 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, since I cannot see what's in front of you, is that the book, the cultural heritage destroyed during shelling in 1991 and 1992? What does it say on that page?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean what does it say at the top?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please pause between answer and question. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at and please tell us, first of all, whether this book recording the damage refers to the complete period of 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this material. I've already said this. And after my expertise in 1991, I no longer participated in further processing. This material was obviously drafted after that, so that I cannot tell you what this document is about, at least as far as my recollection from that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When your first information -- if your first information was 17.5 million and then was later reduced to 5 million, does that mean that the damage shown in the preliminary report was exaggerated?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think you understood me properly. There is a process whereby it was first 5 million, then 17 million, and then the final number was 54. So I think it does not go from 17 to 5, but it goes in the sequence that I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was this? Who told you about that information about 17 million, and when did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found this out unofficially, before I came to The Hague, meaning before 10 or 15 days ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who asked you that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked some of my colleagues from the Institute for Reconstruction, which deals with the operative part and which bears the burden of organising and managing the restoration of Dubrovnik following the destruction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who told you this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was Mr. Vjekoslav Vierda who -- I don't know what his post is at the moment. He was an official from the reconstruction institute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he take part in the assessment of the damage in 1991, 1992?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that he told you that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please tell me: Which period does this damage refer to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't talk about that. In a way, it was just indicated or shown through these two figures, and that was all that I obtained at that time, and I considered that sufficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need this document any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified before the Trial Chamber that in the period that we're discussing, you came to the Old Town once or twice a week in October, November, and December of 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on what I remember. I wasn't keeping a diary, so this is just an approximate statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went to the Old Town, did you go along the walls of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the Franciscan monastery during your visits?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not go to the Franciscan monastery in that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the Dominican monastery?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you pass through the small streets of the Old Town, except for those streets which lead to your mother's house?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mostly focused on getting there as soon as possible, so it was like tunnel movement. I always used the same route. I would go partially along the Stradun, then Od Puca Street, so I would not be exposed -- I would not be seen from Zarkovica, where I would be exposed to sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know where any shell fell and what it damaged in the course of October, November, and December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see the damages on Stradun. I think we're talking about two or three impacts on the sidewalk. And this is what I recall at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned on the 5th of May, when you were asked by my learned colleague - this was on page 11 of the unofficial transcript - that following the shelling in October, you came to the Old Town and then, after the October shelling, you describe that there were fragments of stone everywhere, that there were roof tiles and pieces of the facade strewn all over, that the Boskoviceva Street was damaged in particular. Is that true, what I have just quoted you as saying?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would first like to see the material so that I can connect it all. Boskoviceva Street was also shelled in that period, before the 6th, and I remember very well that there was this rubble there that you described.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 11, you said that on your route from Pile, Stradun, along the Stradun to your mother's, there were fragments of stone everywhere, fallen roof tiles, and facade fragments. This was from the transcript on the 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, "all over the place" is something you can take as a relative description. In that period, particularly in November, there were scores of hits all over town, so it was just something that stuck in my memory during that period, and that is how I described it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you're telling us about October, if I'm not wrong.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm now talking about the period prior to the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, when you say "preliminary report," when you look at a preliminary report, why is the report a preliminary one?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a good question, and I think it will probably give you answers to all your questions about that. A preliminary report is used as a term for something that is subject to certain changes. From the outset, when you begin to work on such material, in a way it's an open situation where details are constantly being added. What we did at that stage was precisely that; we opened up this process, we began it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a final report ever compiled?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us: Why was there such a hurry to complete these preliminary reports?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the reasons, but it was clear, in a way, that this material should be presented to the international public so that such cultural and historic entity should be shown to the world and the damage made to it, so that we could gather the means and the funds in order to restore such a damaged cultural heritage, meaning the whole town. I was not privy to the whole scenario, but we did carry out that project with a great degree of enthusiasm, and we were internally motivated to complete this work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the most important thing that was to be determined in this preliminary report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we were to determine the extent of the damage. We wanted to see what the overall extent of the damage was, and in my assessment, since I am an architect and a planner, to determine the degree of damage, the type of damage we're talking about, and also to see how possible was it to still continue to use those buildings and how we could organise the reconstruction stages gradually, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please provide us with brief answers since we are short of time and we would like to complete your testimony as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As I -- as far as I understood from your questioning so far, or your testimony so far, and based on your answers from my learned friend from Mr. Re, the dates when certain things happened are of secondary importance in relation to the actual extent of the damage and to what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I respond? It's not of secondary importance, but it wasn't of primary importance, or it's not of lesser importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How important was it for you to determine the kind and type of projectiles which caused the damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not so important for us. We just wanted to see what the source of damage was so that we could see what the effects were on the building in terms of the damage that occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interested in the direction where the projectiles came from that caused the damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interested in knowing the characteristics of the shell or other means which caused the damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. It was important for us as previous information, because we knew that, for example, mortar shells had a different kind of damage. It was more of a surface damage, while tank or other types of shells went more deeply, and they caused greater extent of damage. So that our prior knowledge was that, before we set out on our inspections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you know about Howitzer shells?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We simply knew that they were more dangerous than the mortar shells in terms of their post-explosion effect. And I know in my own personal experience that I was most afraid of such tank or cannon grenades or shells. I don't know whether they were Howitzers, I'm not a professional in that sense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In how many places did you find the remains of Howitzer tank or any other kind of shell which hit the town?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you with certainty that it was in one street. This was, I think, in block 11, close to the area next to Strossmayerova Street. We were told that this shell did not explode.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you recognise the remains or the parts of an exploded Howitzer shell?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It makes a narrower crater. That was our kind of estimate. So its impact or energy of impact was much greater. But this is my own interpretation, so please take it with a certain degree of reserve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the damage depend on the angle of impact?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a ballistics expert, so I can't answer that question, but perhaps we could conclude something like that based on what we see on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about impact angles?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do now, but at that time I did not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time when you were drafting the report you didn't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My knowledge of that was very superficial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a police investigation and an on-site investigation conducted by the police about the events that we are discussing here and have been discussing over the past few days?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I don't think so, but I cannot be sure about that. As far as I know, it was not conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your team, did you have a criminal investigations technician, perhaps, who did the investigation to find out how the damage was caused?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that we were the technical team that was supposed to record the technical damage, but we did not deal in the criminal investigation side of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have anybody in your team who was a ballistics technician in order to determine the cause and the manner of the damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we could not allow ourselves such a luxury, in view of the circumstances that we were working in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Replying to a question from my learned friend on May 5th on page 39, you said that the information about when and how a building was damaged was received also from the people who lived there or from neighbours. What did you do in cases where there were no people who actually lived there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly the situation was that the tenant or the neighbours were there. If we were dealing with a building that was burned down completely, then we would hear what the neighbours had to say about it, or from those who happened to be in that building during the shelling but who had taken shelter. Of course, they were not in the building during the shelling itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The buildings that had completely burned down, what did you know about the causes? Why did these buildings burn down completely?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were talking about flammable projectiles, which -- incendiary projectiles which hit the building. We had information about whether this was -- we did not have information whether this happened to be a mortar or a tank shell, so it was not something that was relevant to us at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you claiming that the fires were caused by an incendiary projectile, that they could not have been caused by another type of projectile?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot know that. All that we knew was that the fire was caused by a projectile that had hit the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether you found any remains of any agent that had caused this fire in any of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the completely burned-out buildings? No, we did not find them in any of those buildings. Perhaps in one. That was a building in block 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about totally burned-out buildings.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We did find some traces. This is a building in block 9. It's a ground-floor building, which was completely burned down. We found traces of a yellow powder, a green/yellow powder, at the place where the shell hit. So it was very close to the place where the building burned down, in the immediate contact zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try and find out where exactly the fire started from when a building was hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did establish that the building had burnt down due to a projectile that contained some sort of an incendiary mixture. And mostly the fire usually started from roof down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We will come to the details later on.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I withdraw this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When talking about roofs, you've told us, if I understood you correctly, that even prior to 1991, efforts were made to make the roofings differ in terms of their colour; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the rector's palace renovated?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact answer, but that was one of the vital facilities to be reconstructed after the earthquake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the earthquake.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were looking at the map, that is, the aerial photograph that you've brought here and that was distributed here, we see that the rector's palace has a bright red roof.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same type of a bright red roof can be found on the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Prosecution Exhibit P174.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since there are many buildings here, please make your answers very brief, because this will take, otherwise, a very long time. Please look at the building marked IX-5. Who gave you the information about the time when the building was damaged and the cause of it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, could you just give me the graphic representation of this damage as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that what you have in front of you will suffice. I'm asking you, on the basis of your report, who gave you the information as to when and how this building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may be enough for you, but it does not suffice for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of the report you have in front of you, can you answer my question as to who gave you the information with regard to when and how the building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this comes under the third category, everything that hasn't burned down completely. That's the second and the third category. The fourth category is the mildest one, and this was obtained on the basis of inquiries with tenants and neighbours surrounding the building. That's as far as I can remember. But I can't say specifically for this case whether it was the neighbour or the tenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, you don't know who gave you the information as to the date and cause of damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have enough information for me to remember what the exact situation here was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Ms. Karaman do while inspecting this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was there together with me. She accompanied me, in a way, and was present during our inspection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was what she specifically did during these inspections.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say for this specific building where she was, how far she was from me, what she was doing. She was my technical assistant, as a colleague, she was a member of the team who worked on this specific building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that the building was hit by a 100-millimetre mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we established that on the basis of the size of the crater. Now, as for determining whether it was 120-millimetre or 80-millimetre, that was of less importance for us at the time. But based on the size of the crater that the shell produced, we would draw a conclusion that a heavier calibre must have been at hand here, in this case a 120-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any traces?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the traces in terms of the damage, such as the crater. If you're referring to the remains of the shell, I believe that in this case we found none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the building marked IX-7. For this specific building, you wrote that the remains of the shell were found, the fins or the wings; is that so?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who provided you with the remains of the mine -- of the shell?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tenants of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you say that the remains of the shell were found in that particular building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know from Mr. Brandjolica that he was a music teacher, an older gentleman, and it wasn't really a collection of arms, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any other evidence to prove this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not deal with the forensic processing of it. For us, the fact that the building was hit sufficed. The fact that there was damage incurred, and that based on the character of the damage, it must have been a mortar projectile. We said it was a 92-millimetre here because based on the size of the crater, that's what we concluded. Now, whether this was a 120-millimetre or an 82-millimetre, that was of less importance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the building marked IX-9. Why is there no information as to the time and the date of your inspection?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it must have been a technical mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given that you established that there was indirect damage done, how could you conclude that the damage had been caused by a 120-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because an impact had been established on a neighbouring building, on an adjacent building, which had the same characteristics and on the basis of that and from conversations with the tenants, we concluded that there must have been some sort of a causal link between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you -- how did you make sure that this damage was not made by a light machine-gun or some sort of -- other sort of, for instance, anti-aircraft gun?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that we didn't deal with the ballistics of it, nor with the forensic processing of it, so for the level of our technical expertise on it, what we established here was enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you as to when the building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been either the tenant or the neighbour, although I think in this case it was a tenant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the building XI-11. Did you find any remains in this particular building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, please. I have to find the building first. I don't have it here. You said XI-11?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That is -- sorry; IX-11.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes. Yes, I was here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find the remains of any shell or any other explosive projectile?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, we found none here, but we found traces of it, based on the damage, which indicated the cause of damage. We established that this is where the impact took place. We established the scope of the damage, that is, the surface damage. And we were given additional information from the tenants, as far as I remember from my conversation with Ms. Batinic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at building IX-12, IX-12. Who entered this correction under the column "type of projectile"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with any precision whether it was a typographical error, but I think it's insignificant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of a projectile allegedly produced the damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was our interpretation. Now, whether it was 120-millimetre or 82-millimetre, I've already discussed this earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have not really said with any certainty whether it was the 120-millimetre or the 82-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But who told you that it was either the 120-millimetre or the 82-millimetre projectile?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said earlier that the residents themselves already had some earlier experience from the different scores of hits, and, on the other hand, the traces of damage indicated such a cause of damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who told you this particular information?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not for this specific case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the building IX-13.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have taken a look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any traces of a shell or any other agent in this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I found any. I mean, I personally. But we -- it was something we learned from Mr. Smok. It was in the attic, and I remember that conversation very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from what direction the projectile hit this particular building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here we can read that the building received two hits, one in November and the other on the 6th of December. The one in November, that was actually the building in front that was directly hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about what can be read here. We can all of us read very well. My question was: Do you know where the shell came from, from which direction it came?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not try to establish that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the building IX-17. What building are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what the drift of your question is. Do you want me to show it to you on the map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I don't want you to show it to me. I'm interested in what building it is, in what street -- in the street.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the buildings in that street that we marked with the number 17. I can show it to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you put the house number here?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been a technical error, a typographical error, something that was left out while it was being typed out, and I must say that the report was being typed out in very difficult circumstances. There was no electricity, no -- so it must have been due to that. But I do have the information in the graphical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any traces of a projectile in this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would first have to read this in order to try and refresh my memory. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you read it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, but as I've said, I would first have to try and identify where the building is based on the graphical representation that we have, because we always have the text together with the graphical representation. As I've said, it must have been an error in the textual part, and if there was such an error ever, then we would always consult the graphical representation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand my question? I am asking you whether you found the remains of a projectile.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't remember?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer to you is: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Who told you about the date or the time of the damage incurred?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been the tenants or the neighbours. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it, specifically?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can say this with any certainty at present, but the source of information must have been either the tenants or the neighbours surrounding that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at building IX-18. Did you try and establish the direction from which the projectile arrived in this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, to the extent that we -- when we went up there, we did not try and find out exactly where the impact was, but we tried, in our graphical representation, to establish this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the graphical representation?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the representation of the projectile and the representation of the building. These are the two graphical representations always accompanying the text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the P72 document that we call it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: P172.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please could the witness be shown P172.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what you were looking for?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In part, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else do you need in order to be able to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need a diagram where the position is exactly pointed out, and also our assessment of the damage. It's with the little arrows, so the same criteria were applied and everything is the same, but I simply don't know why this was not included in the material. It would have been faster and easier for you and for me and for the Trial Chamber to be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you know from which direction this projectile came, the one that caused this damage? Just give me a brief answer. There is no need to dwell on this.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, listen. I went to see 63 buildings, and 13 years later, please allow me to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd have to refresh my memory. I'd have to look at this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look at IX-19, please. Where was this building hit from?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to that question. The witness has repeatedly said he was not looking for or trying to assess where the fire was coming from. He said he doesn't know where it was coming from. It wasn't his purpose. My learned friend asked him in relation to every building, where was it hit from. That is different to where was the impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I explain?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the indictment, my client is charged with 450 buildings. It is my right to establish, through putting questions to this witness and any other witness, that this is damage that was caused, allegedly, by operations of units under the command of my client. So if the witness is asked this question and says he doesn't know, then we quickly move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I quite agree, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the projectile came from, the one that allegedly damaged this building IX-19?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The description says on the southern side, the southern facade, the profile stone gutter, and that the damage was caused by shrapnel. So that could be some indication where the projectile could have come from, but I never studied that, or was I involved in that at the time, to see where the projectile came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems that it came from the south, judging by this description.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you have to understand that the town is not placed orthogonally but that its position is somewhat different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about this particular building, IX-19?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been either the tenants or the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it specifically?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at IX-20. Who gave you information about this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the major buildings. These were buildings that figure prominently when the entire town is viewed. So we resorted to personal observation, because we could observe the building even from a distance. Now we can only establish that before the 6th of December, there was no damage on the Orthodox church.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Who provided you with this information?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, our observation was carried out in a similar fashion as it was with regard to other major buildings. So this was personal interpretation, if we can put it that way, because we were able to see for ourselves on the spot, and also even from a distance we could see the roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As far as this building was concerned, was it the priest who explained things to you, as was the case in the Franciscan monastery? Did the priest explain what happened?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we had a situation where, as far as I can remember now, at least a bit, we went to see a gentleman -- I don't know exactly what his position was. He was an orthodox priest, at any rate. And he lives in the street of Izmedju Polaca. When we observed his apartment, we had additional information about this, if I can put it that way, as far as I can remember. I know that together with my colleagues, I talked to the man about his building too, because he had an apartment in town, and I think that at that moment it was even possible from that apartment to see parts of the Orthodox church, especially the roof, parts of the roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did all of that last?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it lasted a bit longer, but on several occasions. What I'm trying to say is that we came and went to the same place several times, and that is how we completed our report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you that because, according to the preliminary report, you spent a total of ten minutes at this particular place, because already at 12.40 you were at IX-21.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This just shows you that at that moment, as we were touring what we could. Because the interior was not accessible to us, we mostly observed things from the outside, and then we returned, and then we learned things indirectly, if I can put it that way, from neighbouring buildings. And we pointed that out, and we see the time span involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the name of the man who gave you this information?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. He is not the only person, because in the neighbourhood there were several persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the name of the other persons who gave you information about the cause and type of damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at X-7. Who told you about the damage sustained by this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the neighbours who told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about the damage specifically?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I just have a moment, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the date when you were purportedly at this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember having been there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How can you remember?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember because this was within my movement through that street, and I don't think that we could have missed this building while we were doing this investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were moving along this street. How do you know that you went to this particular building at number 12?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were. I don't know how I'm supposed to answer this, how do I know that I was at that building. I mean, I did not take any pictures in order to document each and every step I made. So I don't know what this means, how come I know that I was at that building? Well, probably on the basis of this description and all the other information that I signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it in this description that jogs your memory that you actually were there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that street. That's what jogs my memory. And that is what I can be reminded by now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see all the buildings in that street? Did you visit all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. of them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that right now, but systematically we toured all buildings and practically we established whether there had been any damage. As I said already, we systematically went to all buildings, and I told you that at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all buildings in that street damaged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Again, I'd have to look at the diagram.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any remains here? Of shrapnel, that is, at this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this description, I cannot remember exactly, but I can only confirm what was written here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at X-10. On page 75 of the transcript from the 5th of May, in response to a question put by my colleague whether you went to that building, you said: "I don't know exactly, but what is written does point to that."

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. What was the date that you referred to? When did I make this statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 5th of May this year, on page 75, line 4.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in my statement?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the transcript before this Honourable Trial Chamber, page 75, line 4.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to look at this transcript in order to know what this is about. I cannot give you an answer now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am telling you about what you uttered two days ago before this Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I haven't got any transcripts in front of me, and I do not analyse what I said. Could you please be so kind as to tell me: You said on the 5th of May. And as far as I know, it's not May, and what year are we talking about? Was I meeting with the investigators in May 2000?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 5th of May this year, you were in this courtroom, sitting in this same courtroom on that same chair, and you said that.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. If that is what it says, then I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know whether you were there at that building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that I was there. The question was, as far as I can remember, is whether I recognise this building in terms of the damage sustained, and that is the only thing I can remember now, because I don't have any transcript in front of me and I don't have any analysis that I conducted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fortunately, we have a transcript.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no dilemma. I went to that building. I remember that very well. I entered it from the lower door, and I know that, and that is how we recorded it too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about this building, when it was damaged and how and by whom?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said then that it was the neighbours, people who have apartments in the neighbourhood, and that is what we could see at that moment and several times when we tried to deal with this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I ask you who told you about this, that is to say its people who were talking. So if I ask you who told you, then you're going to tell you that you know who told you or that you do not know who told you. So do you know who told you about the damage of this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, I do not know the name and surname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from which direction this building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the photograph that can be ascribed to this facility, the direction cannot be established. The ridge can be seen here, but really, this is not my line of work and I cannot make any comments about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at XI-15. What did you establish at this building as the cause of fire?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we established any causes, but the effects were rather indicative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you about the cause.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the cause is concerned, we didn't establish anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the fire started on this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look. It started from the roof, most probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that it started from the roof?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because in a way it was caused by the impact, and then fire followed. That is also the information that we got from neighbours in other buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you about this specifically?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this your assumption that the fire started from the roof?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an assumption, but it is supported by certain interpretations of the neighbours who were in the immediate vicinity, or tenants.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are the neighbours who said this to you, and what did they tell you exactly?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the names of these people exactly, but I'm just saying that this was the principle according to which we worked, that is to say, putting questions to neighbours. I've said that several times already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were these neighbours? Were they in a shelter when all of this was happening? Did they tell you about that? Or were they standing there and watching what was going on?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically about this building, but they went to the lower parts of the houses, as my mother did. That is to say, those parts that were less open to hits from the air. Since these streets are narrow, I think that this was a realistic assumption, or rather, assessment. And they knew how many impacts came on the basis of detonation, and also what was caused by the impacts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this specific building.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This specific building shares the fate of all of those who burned down, so it doesn't distinguish itself in any particular way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please take a short break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Certainly, Mr. Petrovic. It's a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, we're still on building XI-15. How did you determine that this was a directly hit building with an incendiary bullet or projectile?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the testimony of the neighbours who heard the impact, and that was how we concluded that, besides the damage, the building also burned down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those neighbours see the impact that you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they most probably did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were those neighbours?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do those neighbours live? In which buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the buildings which are in the immediate vicinity of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who those people were?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 5th of May of this year, in this courtroom, why did you say, on page 68, line 25, speaking about the same building, that this category of damage - we're talking about a building that burned down - could have been the result only of a direct hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the other examples also indicated and proved this theory. I'm talking about the buildings that burned down and which I personally saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can fire spread from one building to another?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can go from one building to another, and this was indicated when such was the case. These were partial traces of burning, and I can show you exactly where these examples are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, you didn't say that the neighbours told you that the building burned down as a result of a direct hit, but you said that the damage, meaning that the whole building burned down, was caused by only -- just a direct hit.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we're talking about buildings that burned down completely, we're talking about instances of a direct hit. When we're talking about buildings that -- where the fire carried on or transferred from one building to another, we're talking about partially burned buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other buildings were there cases where they were directly hit but were not burned down, were not set on fire?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any buildings that had incendiary material in them? Did you check that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean when you say "incendiary material" or "flammable material."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any gas cannisters, ammunition, fuel; things like that? Did you check that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not check for things like that, but we did see places where the explosions occurred which bore traces of the yellow-green powder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And why is that not stated in this report about the building that burned down that we're looking at right now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this building burned down completely and the information that we put here was sufficient for us to determine the type of damage that was inflicted and the potential source, based on our experience of the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that this -- how do you know that this building, XI-15, did not contain explosives or petrol?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that we were not conducting a criminal investigation and that this level of information was sufficient for us, the information that is stated here, as well as the information about the cause of the building burning down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that this building was not set on fire?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've told you that we were not carrying out a criminal investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you allow the suggestion that these buildings were set on fire on purpose?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not encounter such cases because the tenants would definitely know if this was the case; if not the tenants, then those who were the immediate neighbours would know of something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you differentiate between a deliberate fire and an explosion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in our specific case, this difference was not relevant; it was only a question of whether the building burned down or not, and that the most probable cause was a hit by an incendiary projectile, a projectile carrying incendiary agents, and that in some way this caused the subject damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you rule out other possibilities of why the building burned down?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot rule them out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it could be the case that this was a deliberate fire?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say whether it was so or not. It's possible that there was some flammable materials in the house, so this could have caused an even greater fire following the initial impact, but the actual first fire could have only been caused by a projectile hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you still standing by that even though that you didn't find any traces of projectiles?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not conduct a criminal investigation. We did not dig among the debris. So it was not possible to go through all of this debris. There were piles of it. It's possible that the debris also contained remains of exploded shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you didn't look for those remains and you didn't find them.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not able to do that. This was a situation in which it was impossible to dig through the rubble in order to look for evidence to see what the real cause was, whether it was a mortar or a 120-millimetre shell or an 85-millimetre. This was something that could not have been done for reasons of time constraints, for practical reasons, and also for reasons that had to do with safety.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the house marked as the house -- the Grbic house was the location of the Belgrade Beko shop?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was a shop on the corner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that that shop burned down that day?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was part of the building in the Od Puca Street, where I didn't go out on inspection. But I remember it quite clearly. We're talking about the Grbic house, which burned down to the ground, including this -- these premises that you're asking me about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the building across the street housed a shop of the Titograd textile company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that building also burned down to the ground?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I was not in charge or I didn't process that block, so I don't have that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the building next to the festival palace, Od Sigurate number 1, housed a shoe shop of Obuca Belgrade and that also burned down?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information is not something that I am aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the house in Od Puca 11, which belonged to the Serbian church district, also housed a shop called Srbin, and that also burned down?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it a little bit strange that out of the six buildings that burned down, four of those buildings were buildings which housed shops or business spaces or premises of companies from Serbia or Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I did not check that kind of statistical information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please look at building XI-16. Who told you about the damage on this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got our information in the same way, by directly viewing the damage. This was done by the team that inspected the building and also they interviewed the neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you when this building was hit? Do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the first and last name of the person, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe more closely who it was?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which building we're talking about. If it's possible, I would like to identify it on the map and then I could recall exactly what building we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P172, unless he already has it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have the graphic image. I only have the text. This is the corner building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking you if you can describe to us who provided this information to you. So could you please focus on that in your answer. To describe more closely, since you don't know exactly who it was, to just give us more details about who it was.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot recall the entire procedure. It's impossible, I think, for anybody to do that, unless this was documented in some other way, filmed by camera or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much. If you don't know, then that is all right. Do you know from which direction this object was -- this building was hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know the direction of the impact, but based on the damage, you can see potentially the direction that the shell came from. But we didn't really consider that, so I cannot give you the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at building XI-17. Who told you about the damage on this building?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the neighbour's from buildings 18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who it was. I know that this building housed the apartment of Mrs. Bibica. I remember that very well. This is an older lady. It was very cold, and she was just receiving her meals. I remember her very well. She was an infirm old lady in a large apartment, which, luckily, was not damaged. And I think we were talking with her cousins. They were helping her. And I remember that conversation very well. I also remember a conversation there with a colleague of mine who actually lives in block 19, which borders on this one. And I also talked with his mother. And that is where we received this information from that you're just talking about now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those two old ladies explained that this was hit by 120-millimetre mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this lady, Mrs. Bibica, was not the one who told us that, but there were two or three younger persons who were actually helping her, whereas my mother's -- my colleague's mother is a very healthy, lively lady, and she could have told us about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old do you think she was?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think she was in her 70s.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this lady in her 70s explained to you that this building was directly hit with two incendiary projectiles of 120-millimetre calibre, mortar shells?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that same building, there is an attic apartment where a relatively young woman lived with her father, and she also was able to testify as to what we are talking about. So we were able to confirm our information to quite an extent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dear Mr. Vukovic, everything that you have been telling us for the past three days is pure improvisation. Mr. Vukovic, this is a building which was completely demolished. There is no apartment of Mrs. Bibica. There is no longer any attic apartment. Everything that you are saying you are improvising. Please, can you look at that.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, may I tell you something about what you have said about improvisation. Improvisation perhaps is something that we're using in order to recall something, but Mrs. Bibica's apartment covers 18 and 19. This is also the case of the attic apartment, and if you can show me a photograph, I will tell you exactly which building we're talking about. But what you are talking about is building 17, and we are finding out information about 17 from these other buildings. So we're not improvising here. We're talking about fact, and the record speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in these two virtual apartments?
