utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not just two apartments. There were --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I withdraw my comment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described conversations with two old ladies. How long did those conversations last?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning Mrs. Bibica, I think we spoke with her on several occasions. One time the conversation was a little longer. We even had tea, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These ladies, one of them infirm and the other in her 70s, on the 6th of December, the town is being shelled, and they are on duty observing, looking, and noting down; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you at all familiar with the situation prior to the 6th and on the 6th in all these apartments in the town? If I may ask this counter-question to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please answer my questions at the moment.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not awaiting that, but they sensed what was to happen. I told you already that every hit would first hit your heart and then the roof of your building. So they were very well aware of what was happening in their town and in the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were aware of the fact that these were two incendiary mortar shells of 120-millimetre calibre?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They heard the number of impacts, the explosions, and it was our estimate that it might have been the mortar shell or an 82-millimetre shell or something similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any traces? Did you at all look for them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. But if we happened to find them, then --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about this specific building.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which? 17, 18, or 19?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've told you clearly. We're talking about the building XI-17. We've been talking about it all along and you are very well aware of it. Od Puca number 11. So did you in that particular building find any specific remains of a projectile?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the case here is similar to that in number 19. This was just a pile of rubble. And we did not go on to investigate the projectile directly involved in this hit. We didn't go through the remains. We saw that the building burnt down, and based on our interviews with the neighbours, we inquired --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you about the remains.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not find them and we did not look for them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you establish the direction from which the damaging projectile arrived?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. I think that according to this description, we can see that it was hit at the northern facade. Now, of course, we should verify as to what "north" means in this case, because we don't have the orientation here, and it would enable me to give you a more precise answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is one of those buildings for which you told us yesterday that you did not dwell on them at all, since the buildings have completely burnt down. This is something you've told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in terms of investigating its interior. We viewed the building from the outside and then made our conclusions on the basis of what we saw looking at it from immediate vicinity and from the buildings immediately adjacent to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you how it was possible that on the 16th [as interpreted] of December you were present at three different buildings at 11.00, you offered as an explanation the fact that for those buildings that had completely burnt down you did not linger there at all.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because the only thing that we could conclude was from what we saw from outside. We concluded that the building had burnt down, and then from subsequent contacts with the people from the neighbouring buildings that had not shared the same fate, we would learn more about the impact itself. There were even traces on the facade that would provide some indications, visual indications, as to the impact of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you in any of the reports state the source, the persons you received information from, the name of a particular neighbour or a bystander who watched the shells fall, or the name of a tenant, or anyone? Is there anywhere any annotation of that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that there is. We put it in brackets. It was the information we learnt at the time and that we did not think was very important. We did not conduct any police investigations that would require us to have in a written form the source of the information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, for you it was sufficient to have a 70-year-old lady say that two shells had fallen and that this was a fact that you could then simply put into your report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wasn't the only indication. It was one of the indications and it wasn't the exclusive source of information that we deemed relevant at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this building, was there a shop held by a Serb?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this with any certainty, because I did not keep that sort of statistical data, either prior to that moment or afterwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Please take a look at the building XI-24. Who had told you how this damage came about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this is a smaller building which wasn't really on our way when moving around the town. So I cannot say with any precision, but I believe that this was the case of us inquiring with the neighbours and possibly with a tenant, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course you don't know who you talked to or who you obtained information from?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know their names, but I know that we got the information from conversations with them, among other things. I think this is one of those examples where, as far as I remember, we found traces of a shell, of an unexploded shell. It was 24, 23, or 22. I'm not sure because they're all very small buildings, but I'm certain that it was in that area, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please tell me: What does this estimate of the area mean, 12-25 square metres? So what sort of an estimate is that, from 12 to 25 square metres? This is double the size of -- the 25 square metres is double the size of 12 square metres.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This might even be a typographical error, from 12 to -- it must have been 20 to 25. But I'm certain that this was the area of that particular building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you measure the area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would visually make an estimate with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make a diagram of it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take any photographs?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not us personally, but as I've said, there was a colleague of ours who, based on our information, would go to photograph some of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know from which direction this particular building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember at this time. I don't think we investigated this, this information for this particular building, just as we didn't for any other building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the building XI-42. Who told you about this particular damage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same situation; we inquired after this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who provided the information?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the name exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you come to the conclusion, given that it is stated here that it is an indirect hit of a mortar shell of 120 and 80 -- 82-millimetre, how did you come to the conclusion as to the type of the hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we concluded here that it was an indirect hit, that the building was damaged due to the shrapnel coming from the impact on one of the neighbouring buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you differentiate between the shrapnel of a shell, of a mortar shell of 120 millimetres and of a mortar shell of 82 millimetres? How do you differentiate between the two, based on the shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we don't conclude that on the basis of the shrapnel. It's not the shrapnel that would indicate the size of the shell. It would rather be the traces of a shell on the neighbouring building, and we interpreted it as having been made by those two projectiles. That is, based on the traces of the impact of a 120-millimetre shell and an 82-millimetre shell, we came to the conclusion that they could have been the causes of damage on this particular building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you of course differentiate between the shrapnel of a 120-millimetre shell and an 82-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you did not understand what I said. We did not conclude that on the basis of the shrapnel but on the basis of the impact that ricochetted and hit this particular building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where is it stated in your report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an explanation for you to try to let you know how we came to the conclusion, but we didn't have the luxury of explaining in a police fashion the entire process to establish the ballistic and forensic information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your estimate, how many shells landed on the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, nor did I investigate that type of statistics. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone was killed in any of the buildings within the Old Town on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside a building, I don't know. I did not analyse such data. I only know that my friend Pavo Urban got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically: Do you know of anyone having been killed in his own building in the Old Town on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any such information, nor am I informed about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether on the 6th of December, in any of the buildings in the Old Town in Dubrovnik, anyone had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of a conclusion would you draw based on what I'll tell you now: That no one was wounded, no one got killed in any of the buildings in the Old Town on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to it on the basis of the relevance of the witness's opinion, based upon facts which my learned friend has put to the witness. That's a matter for the determination of the Trial Chamber. It is unclear what the purpose of the question is. And it only invites, in my submission, speculation from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- question, Mr. Petrovic, invites pure speculation by the witness. He does not purport to be qualified to speak in any way about such a question. You're putting something to him which you should in the end perhaps be putting to us. We may not be qualified, but we may have to decide the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The gist of what I wanted to achieve was to ask an expert for the damage whether he had noticed anywhere the type of damage that could have caused the death or wounding of anyone within a building in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that each and every impact was a potential threat to the people who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How are you able to know anything about -- and do you know anything about the removal of rubble from the streets of the Old Town in October and November 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about it in any detail. I only know that the streets were being cleared up in order to ensure that they are passable. I even think that Boskoviceva Street had been boarded up so that people would avoid it, because there was the danger of some construction material falling down from the roofs. That's what I know. And I know that the protection of the cultural and historical heritage was done by boarding up these buildings. And this is the only thing that I can tell you now in relation to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us: What are the dimensions, approximate dimensions, of the largest part of a stone facade or a roof, part of a roof or part of the pavement that you were able to see as rubble in the streets of the Old Town at that period?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you also refer to the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after the 6th. Well, the largest piece.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. How many that you could see in the street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I don't know if you need the length, if you need the area. Well, approximately one metre or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One metre in length?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe that was the case of a balustrade in front of the St. Blaise's. I can't tell you exactly, because I didn't really keep the statistical data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that the largest piece you saw was one metre in length?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. That's my estimate, with hindsight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. Were we able to see yesterday and the day before this balustrade of the St. Blaise's in the video clips shown in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've told you that this is my faint memory of it, but I did see it in the Franciscan monastery, in the Boskoviceva Street, and in other places. I don't recall exactly where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As for all the rest you saw, it is smaller than the dimensions you referred to just now, considerably smaller?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But most of this was smashed into pieces. I should say that it is the type of effect that one sees after a fire, when an entire construction goes down, and then the type of rubble and the dimensions that you refer to are quite different. But what I saw here, it is approximately within that order of magnitude, including that, so smaller ones, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell us the following, then: What was it, then, that had obstructed Stradun in terms of free passage for cars and pedestrians on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we've seen it on footage, and I can say that again: It is pieces of buildings and furniture, different types of debris, then also parts of tiles, roof tiles; then -- it was the type of material that simply made these big heaps in the middle of the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How high were the heaps?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, it is hard for me to say. Sometimes they were smaller and sometimes they were bigger. But if you're asking about the range, it was, say, from 10 to 15 centimetres up to, say, half a metre, a metre. It depended on the cause of the damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Stradun, on the 6th and 7th, where was there debris and rubble in a heap of half a metre, as you had put it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, primarily in front of the buildings that were, in a way, that had burned down. So, in a way, as far as I can assess now, or as far as I can remember now, that would be the place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's these two buildings, the festival building, the festival palace, and also the other one near it, Od Sigurate number 1?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in part, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, then: What was it that prevented you and other pedestrians from moving about? What prevented vehicles from moving about, as you testified in this courtroom two days ago?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said. These were pieces that were there in the street. So it was obstructed passage. It was difficult to move about. I told you that because that was my impression. Quite simply, movement had been considerably hampered in relation to what it was like usually in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about the removal of rubble on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The removal of rubble, I don't know anything about it directly, and on the 6th, anyway, nothing could be removed. What was being done was fires that were being put out. It was dark. It was impossible to intervene. So the rubble that we are referring to now, in my estimate, at least where I moved about, was not a primary concern. Its removal was not. What people focused on was putting out the fires. So when entering town in this night-time atmosphere, that is what I managed to observe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I please have the following document distributed. It is a document which was submitted to the Defence the night before last. It is part of the document concerned. As our colleagues informed us only last night, about 7.00, this is a document that was submitted by this witness who is now testifying before you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. If I could just correct the record. It was not last night. We turned it over the first day of cross-examination, or just before cross-examination, I believe. There is a record of receipt. There was -- a telephone call was made by Ms. McCreath to the Defence and left in their locker. The day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you permit, it was the night before last, around 1800 hours. Could you please consult your case manager. The night before last. That was the 5th of May, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Right. Night before last. I believe the initial suggestion was last night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If counsel are conducting a private debate, they should not do it in this court.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This has happened before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Apologise, Your Honour. It was directed to the Chamber so the Chamber would understand that it was to correct the record as to when the information that was given to us was turned over. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Whether either of you are correct is not of particular concern. What is apparently clear is that a document was handed over at very late notice. The issue is: What is it, and what's its relevance? Are you going to explore that with the witness? Or if you are, go ahead, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My observation primarily had to do with my regret regarding the fact that I could present this to you in the English language. That is the primary reason why I made any reference to it. Otherwise, regrettably, we are used to having material disclosed to us at a very late date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, did you hand this document over, the one that we're talking about, the one that is before you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did hand it over, but that was my very own assessment, my very subjective assessment, in terms of the presentation of that material that I thought would be relevant in terms of the interpretation of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to read on page 2 the heading that is there, and then I'm going to put a question to you. Could you please read the heading for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The location of direct --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please slow down. The interpreters do not have this document. Could it be placed on the ELMO, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you'd pause a moment, Mr. Vukovic, we'll get the document into a position where it can be seen by the interpreters, which will help the process considerably. It may mean you'll have to turn a little to read it. I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, would you please be so kind as to read this again, but slower, of course, the heading of this document.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Localities of direct impacts by projectiles during the shelling of the historical nucleus of Dubrovnik, October, December 1991."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: November.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have another document placed before Mr. Vukovic, namely, P63, tab -- Your Honour, my colleague has informed me -- Your Honour, my colleague --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are just confused by a translation or an interpretation a moment ago. Is the date in the heading October to December, October to November?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, October, November. October, November. It's a mistake in the interpretation. And that can be done by the interpreters themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that they tried to correct it immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That was the effect that was done and that's what made us doubtful for a moment. We're all of the one mind. Now, Mr. Petrovic, you had a query.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to ask for another document now. Could we leave this document before the witness, and could the witness please be given P63, tab 6, annex 3. Along with that document, that is. Your Honour, this is a report. This is a report of UNESCO experts about the damage sustained by the Old Town in the months of October and November 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, do you have this in a language you understand, this document that I referred to just now?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is all, all of this that I have before me now, if that is what you want me to confirm, then yes, I have got it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's just annex 3 of a very voluminous document which, for reasons of practicality, we put before you. Otherwise, everyone in this courtroom is fully familiar in detail with the content of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P174 is no longer needed, so perhaps you can remove it from the witness's table so there's not too much material there. [In English] Mr. Usher, please leave the document which is list of report of war destruction. Just leave the document on the ELMO. We just do not need any more this binder P174.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vukovic, while --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, would you like me to pause, if needed? It is document P63, tab 6, annex 3, that accompanies the report. In the original, the document is in the French language, and we have translations into English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for pausing, Mr. Petrovic. We've caught up with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, could you please give me very brief answers to the next set of questions since we have a very large number of buildings that we have to go through. Is it correct that the day before yesterday, when looking at the so-called Grbic video, on page 22 of the transcript, 36:04 - that's the second of the footage involved - did you say that that was Siroka Street and the damage in Siroka Street? Just give me a brief answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In annex 3, on page 6 of annex 3, or rather -- just a moment, please. On page 7 of annex 3, do you see, under numbers 25 and 26, information about two houses in Siroka Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it. It is numbers 25 and 26.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Under number 30 in the document that you handed over to us, that's the document that's on the ELMO -- the document is on the ELMO, Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, you mean this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 30, you see yet again information about damage in Siroka Street numbers 5 and 8 respectively?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at this. Yesterday, when watching the so-called Jokic video, which is P145, at 0 minutes, 8 seconds, page 38 of the transcript, did you show us the damage on the Sponza Palace?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that particular moment now exactly, but if that entered the transcript, then it is possible that what you're saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that you provided to us, under number 9, do you see the Sponza Palace?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In annex 3, on page 1, under number 6 is the Sponza Palace also noted there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, in watching the Jokic video footage yesterday, at minute 1:20, 1:37, 1:38, page 40 of the transcript, did you not show us the damage in Boskoviceva Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your document, under number 17 and 18, do you see the buildings in Boskoviceva 1 and Boskoviceva 3?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17 and 18. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 5 of the annex that you have in front of you, under number 18, and on page 6, under A, B, C, and D, do you see the damage at Boskoviceva 1, Boskoviceva 3, Boskoviceva 2, and Boskoviceva 4?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these buildings at the beginning? As a matter of fact, they are corner buildings of Boskoviceva and Stradun?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The description is quite detailed and quite reliable, so what it says here and what you say is more or less the true location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, on page 41 of the transcript, Jokic video P145, at 1 minute, 44 seconds, did you not show us the damage on houses which are on the corner of Stradun and Dropceva Street, describing that these were houses on the corner of Stradun and Dropceva in the direction of Prijeka Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at your document now, under number 20, residential building Dropceva 2.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a corner building on Stradun and Dropceva Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at annex 3 now, on page 6, under number 20. Do you see the words "Dropceva number 2" there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, in this same Jokic video, P145, third minute, at 3 minutes, 20 seconds, did you not show us the damage in Siroka Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to look at that footage, because I cannot recall everything that I said, where it was in the footage and at what minute. I would have to remind myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which building did you identify at 3 minutes, 20 seconds in P145 in Siroka Street?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In looking at the same footage, P145, did you not point out to us the courtyard of the Franciscan monastery?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier today, earlier today, did you not tell us that during the period that we're talking about, you did not enter the courtyard of the Franciscan monastery?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you didn't know what the courtyard of the Franciscan monastery looked like, for example, on the 5th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to give you a more detailed answer here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please respond whether you personally were there and saw the state of the courtyard of the Franciscan monastery before the 5th of December or on the 5th of December, 1991, and did you see what it looked like?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That particular example is not something that I saw personally, but I heard from others about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, at 5 minutes, 17 seconds -- from 5 minutes to 17 seconds to 6 minutes, 54 seconds of the JNA video, you showed us what the Franciscan monastery looked like, the courtyard and the other buildings of the Franciscan monastery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just showing you what I was seeing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your document, under number 27, do you see the Franciscan monastery complex? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In annex 3, page 8, under number 35, does it say and do you see it, the Franciscan monastery? Does it state that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, at the JNA video at 7 minutes, 32 seconds, did you not show us the damage on the Minceta tower?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that interpretation is not correct. I did not say that Minceta was the subject of my inspection, and I did not record the damage there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 40 of your list, do you see that it states Minceta tower?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the same video, at 10 minutes, 25 seconds, you pointed out the library, the Franciscan monastery library, for us.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us that it had suffered a direct hit. How did you know that the library of the Franciscan monastery suffered a direct hit?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the library had suffered a direct hit, but the roof of the block suffered a direct hit, where the library is located. That would be the correct interpretation of what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the question of how do you know that this was on the 6th of December, you said that it was on the 6th of December for sure because if it had not occurred on that day, it would have already been cleared. And I'm talking about the rubble, the mortar that you can see, the plaster in that footage.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because this facility is too important for me not to know something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when the footage was recorded that we saw yesterday, P145?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know if what we saw yesterday is what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when this footage was filmed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While looking at the same video, P145, at 14 minutes, 59 seconds, did you not point out the damage for us on the walls near the Pile gate?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the walls near the Pile gate the western section of the wall?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The walls have their eastern and their western sections, so in relation to the position of the town, this is the western section of the walls.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see on your list, under number 39, the western walls of the city?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In annex 3, page 5, under number 17, do you see a description of the damage of the Pile gate there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see. I need to give you a clarification. My interpretation, based on the footage yesterday, referred to the passable walkways on the upper part of the walls, and we did not discuss the gate. The actual location is above the gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same footage, did you not tell us yesterday -- actually, it was the day before. I apologise. Not yesterday. At 17 minutes and 33 seconds, indicate to us the damages around the St. Blaise's tower?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention the St. Vid tower, but I did say that it was the northern part of the walls, if I'm interpreting what you're trying to say properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I wanted to ask you. Under number 41 on your list, the northern section of the walls, at Buz, or Buza.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is that section.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at annex 3, on page 10, one line before last -- no. I apologise. The very last line. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That it states there the northern part of the wall from Buza?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says there that that was the gate, but there it says the northern sector of the walls at Buza. So this would be a more specific reference to that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and it supports what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am not sure whether in my testimony yesterday or the day before I talked about that specific location or a place that was a little bit farther away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, at 9.42, on the footage of P145, at 18 minutes, 35 seconds you showed us two holes in the roof of the Dominican monastery.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 8 on your list, do you see the Dominican monastery?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please now look at annex 3, page 1, under number 4, the Dominican monastery.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, at 9.50 a.m., you showed us on the footage P145, at 20 minutes and 4 seconds, a hole on the wall of Mali Arsenal, the Small Arsenal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I wasn't following you. Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, while viewing footage of Exhibit P145 at 20 minutes, 4 seconds, did you not show us a hole in the roof of the Small Arsenal?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your list, under number 7, do you see the Small Arsenal?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In annex 3, page 10, under number 1, do you see that the -- it states the Small Arsenal facility?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, at 9.55 a.m. -- 9.53 a.m., in footage of Exhibit P145, at 20 minutes, 34 seconds, did you not point out the Large Arsenal, the Gradska Kavana, the city cafe, with a hole in its roof?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at your list under number 4 and see if it does not state the Arsenal there.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at annex 3, page 4, number 8. Does it not describe the Large Arsenal?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we can, perhaps we could go on our break now. This is a good time, if you agree. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, would you be so kind as to tell us if yesterday, while viewing the video P145, at 21 minutes, you described the damage at the old port, at the entrance to the old port in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the question? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is as follows: Whether yesterday, while you were viewing the P145 at 21 minutes, you described the damage at Veliki Valobran or Veliki Mul.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are two different things. If you mean at Veliki Mul, that is the pier, whereas the Valobran is another thing. I was talking about Veliki Mul, where the ships dock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at your list, under number 5.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, and I see it says "Veliki Mul."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to look at annex 3, page 10, under number 5. Here it also mentions Veliki Mul as having been damaged.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Veliki Valobran here, and I don't know what that is, that the projectile hit the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't Veliki Mul and Veliki Valobran one and the same thing?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There must have been an error in the translation. Where -- there was ever a bench there at Veliki Valobran or is there a bench actually at the pier, at Veliki Mul?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume. We also have Porporela, which is another of these piers there, and there is also a bench there, but I can't really seem to find a connection between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please take a look at the list of the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments. Under number 10, it reads there that the town bell tower --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was damaged in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the list, it also reads that the Jesuit church, the church of St. Ignatius, had also been damaged, and that's under number 14, and that's in the period of October and November 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the building that you marked at this aerial photograph yesterday, this aerial photograph of the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under number 32, contained in the list of the locations of direct hits incurred during the shelling of Dubrovnik in October and November 1991, also read Rupe granary, that is, the Rupe museum.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've also marked this location on the aerial photograph that you were placing some marks on.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document specifying the locations of direct hits in the period of October and November, does it include the town port and the St. Ivan fortress under number 3 -- under numbers 2 and 3?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell us the following: The document that you've brought and given to the Prosecution, is it the report on the destruction of Dubrovnik in October and November 1991, made by the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean this particular material that comes behind this cover page, then my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D81.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, is it true that, apart from the buildings contained in the document P174, which bears your signature as a person who established the damage, you are unable to confirm with any certainty when the damage was made to any other buildings in the Old Town in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am able to confirm this only for some of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that in relation to the buildings that we dealt with in the latter part of the examination, you have no direct knowledge as to what the condition of this building was prior to the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any detailed information, but I am referring to those buildings where it was evident, evident because of the significance of the building and the information that I was able to obtain with regard to those, and it was for those buildings that I was able to establish this with certainty. Now, as for the other buildings, I wasn't even involved in any detailed examination of those, nor did I dispose of the information that could indicate that particular information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, the buildings that you inspected, you're not actually claiming that they were damaged on any given date, apart from just saying that they were damaged.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all the indications pointed to the fact that it must have happened on the 6th, but even had I not been present on-site and viewing the buildings, I was able to reach this conclusion based on the knowledge of the degree of damage incurred on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see any of the damage, nor did you record any information related to that, nor did anyone else record it; isn't it true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not record it in the sense in which you're asking me, but I'm referring you back to what I said earlier: The conclusions I was able to make, I was able to make them based on the information present at the site that I inspected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these conclusions, on the basis of the remains that were shown to you were actually made on the basis of these two video footages that you saw?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and on the basis of what I was able to find out during my visits to the Old Town after the shelling, and when I was able to confirm when moving along Stradun as -- and identify as recent damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell us -- just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true that, in relation to many pieces of information contained in your report P174, that for many of them you said that they contained typographical errors?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only in relation to the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this an official document that was supposed to be used to show the causes, the degree, and the time when the damage was incurred?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the preliminary report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come there are no corrections if there are, as you say, so many typographical errors in many places?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in the compilation of the final version, if indeed there is any final version. I know that in the process of the reconstructions of these facilities, many amendments were made to the report in terms of the degree of damage, the cost of reconstruction, and that would be it in relation to that issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can any of the contents of the report be matched? Do they tally, indeed, your original notes?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part related to the specific site, the specific building, and with regard to the degree of damage specified there --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to answer my question. Can we match any of the contents of the report that is P174 with any of your work products, any of your notes that you submitted to the institute? Can we match them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you can, but if you ask me, I would actually be able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, please do.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what you mean -- what you want me to answer specifically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where are the original records of your inspections?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You should ask my colleagues in the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments whether they actually filed the material anywhere. I didn't need the material subsequently, and I didn't inquire after it, and I don't know if they actually filed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A typographical error of 12 to 25 square metres, you said that was a typographical error just a moment ago when we were going through that relevant document. This typographical error is substantial. It is very important for the determination of the cost of damage.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it is not of such a nature that one could draw a general conclusion -- that one couldn't draw a general conclusion based on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether there was a shelter in the Old Town in Dubrovnik in October, November, and December 1991.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes; as far as I know, there were two shelters. I don't know if there are any other ones. I won't speak, of course, of those shelters in individual buildings like the one where my mother was, but I know that there was one in the St. Ivan, St. John fortress, and in the Revelin fortress. Those were the two shelters that I'm aware of. Now, I can't vouch for shelters in individual houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In most of your answers, you stated that you received information from neighbours. Where were the owners of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to be aware of the nature of ownership at the time. If you're referring to the apartments themselves, this is an entirely different matter that requires a different answer. If by saying "owners," you mean owners of business premises, then I wouldn't be able to tell you specifically about the owners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me where the persons who resided in those buildings were if most of the information you got you actually got from the neighbours. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. And what I already said was that at the time, the people were already returning to their apartments to see what the situation was like. Some of the flats were damaged, others weren't. Parts of them weren't. They tried to be present there during the identification of the damage in order to be able to restore, to make these flats of theirs habitable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come the neighbours remained in their apartments whereas those you're talking of in these reports went elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation varied. Of course, the buildings that have completely burnt down, their tenants couldn't go back. But as for those falling in the categories 2, 3, 4, as they were returning home, one could contact the owners of the apartments, and of course the neighbours were those who shared similar fate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who went to the shelters, then?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shelters were used when the alarm was sounded, and we were trying to obtain information when we could contact the people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were those alarms sounded at the time when the town was shelled?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think so. Now, who went to the shelters and when, I can't say. I know for sure that my mother did not go to these shelters, but I can't say for the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask for another document to be distributed, which is both in English and in Serbian. It's a document which, under Rule 65 ter, had been disclosed to the Defence under number 350. It's an excerpt from the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Vukovic, tell us: Is this a report of the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments that we have been talking about all this while?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this document. This is an excerpt from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The cover page, does it match what -- does it look like the cover page usually made by the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it about it that makes you suspicious about it being a document of the Institute for the Protection of Monuments?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer this question because I don't know what the title -- the headings of the usual correspondence of the institute looked like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony, you talked about the aerial bombing; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But could you be more specific with regard to the locations that I mentioned in that context.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't you see the JNA aircraft bombing Srdj?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Not only aircraft, but also the gunships, from the sea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doesn't the description of what you saw -- isn't the description of what you saw read on page 2 of this document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I cannot confirm the time because I did not keep any records of that. I know that it was before the 6th of December. But whether it was on the 6th of December itself is something I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is D82.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, how did you manage not to get drafted into the Croatian army in October, November, December 1991?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an architect, just like my other colleagues, I was supposed to be at my regular job, and we were supposed to take care of the material there. That was the reason why, actually, things were not the way you had put it, why I did not join up from the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you leave the town of Dubrovnik if you wanted to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean in that period?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean in that period.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember any more, but I think it was increasingly difficult to leave. If you're asking me about my experience in this regard, I had no wish or intention of leaving, but I did care about my wife and my young daughter. I wanted them to go to a safer place. They went on the Marina ship, like many others did, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to get out at all?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never even thought of it. The thought never crossed my mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did it never cross your mind to leave town with your wife and daughter?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't want to leave because I had a feeling that finally reason would prevail and that there would be no lethal situations like the one that occurred on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all able-bodied men prevented from leaving Dubrovnik? Were they forbidden to leave Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see a person in uniform in the Old Town of Dubrovnik ever?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember ever having seen anyone in uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone carrying out the duties of a policeman in the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see an armed person in the Old Town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I cannot remember any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of anyone passing through the town of Dubrovnik or staying in the town of Dubrovnik with weapons?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not interested in this type of information, and I am not in a position to answer your question, as you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, thank you very much for your cross-examination, and particularly the purpose which kept very much to the point and therefore very much within time. Thank you. Yes. Perhaps before I turn to you, Mr. Re, you might assist me, if you would, please, with the document which you have been dealing with, that which was the report of war destruction for October and November and the localities of direct impacts. Is this a document you had any part in the preparation of? That's the document that is probably on the list in front of you. I'm referring to Exhibit D81, the two pages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not have this document before you, but I do know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it something that you were involved in the preparation of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Were you aware of it when you conducted your examinations of buildings, inspections of buildings, in December of 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for this document, in such a way, no. But I did have some preliminary information from my colleagues with whom we exchanged information in the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments before actually going to the localities that were inspected on the 6th, or rather, after the 6th. At least, I availed myself of this type of information, to a large extent, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Re. Re-examined by Mr. Re:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to continue in relation to that particular exhibit, D81, when did you obtain that document?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obtained this document before I came to The Hague, so perhaps a week prior to my departure. Since I asked for photocopies to be made for me of the material that this institution had, notably for the buildings where I carried out the inspections. I did not have any private documentation of my own. Along with that, I obtained this document, which I saw for the first time. I thought that it was of interest, for me, and as far as I can see now, it is of interest for the Prosecution and for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your cross-examination, I think it was today, Mr. -- It was earlier today, Mr. Petrovic asked you about your visiting the Old Town before the 6th of December to see your mother, and you talked about taking back routes to avoid sniper fire. Do you know whether anyone was injured in sniper fire, injured by sniper fire in that period?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of a particular example, but I heard that a man had been hit at the Pile gate. But whether that is correct or not is something that I cannot confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that why you were taking these precautions?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely for that reason, that we knew that Stradun was an open target from Zarkovica. Quite simply, we tried not to be out in the open, in terms of any kind of equipment that could be used for an attack, a sniper, whatever. But at any rate, there was a danger involved, and therefore, we did exercise caution when we went to town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic also cross-examined you about a paragraph in your statement which contained the date of the 13th of December. I think you more or less corrected that in your examination-in-chief to the 10th of December, based upon the -- your first inspections of buildings. My question is: When did you first discover this error in the date in your statement?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I discovered that only recently, and I must say that this happened after I had made my statement. I think I discovered that just before I left, or perhaps a month before that, when the gentlemen of the investigation came to speak with me in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bring it to the attention of the Office of the Prosecution staff at that point?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic also asked you a number of questions about your mother's address, and street numbering, I could say in general, in the Old Town of Dubrovnik. You told the Trial Chamber in examination-in-chief that you were born and raised in the Old Town. How do people in the Old Town refer to addresses and places where people live, and shops and other objects there?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a good question. Actually, our custom in town has to do with visual identification of a particular place, not statistics like house numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do people commonly use street names -- sorry, addresses, such as 4 Od Puca, or 5 Stradun or 6 Izmedju Polaca in describing where they live or where they're going to?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We resorted to visual identification. I'm talking about the period when we went to inspect certain localities. We would identify the small stone plaques at the door, at the entrance, and that was the number identifying the houses that we came to inspect. So in line with that, we wrote down certain information that had to do with addresses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm just talking generally. The practice in the Old Town of how people refer to where they live and if they're going to visit a friend or directing a person to a certain place, are street numbers used?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said: Visual identification is what is resorted to, as far as I can say, but I cannot speak on behalf of everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P174, which is the index and the ... And also Exhibit D80, and also Exhibit D79, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: D79 is the exhibit on which you have marked your mother's house. Don't do anything at the moment. I actually wish you to mark where the doorway is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would it be appropriate to mark on this Defence exhibit or does Your Honour wish me to provide another identical copy of the same document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't see -- I don't have yet that exhibit. I think it might be minimising the chance of confusion if there was a separate identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please give that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, I want you to look at an identical copy of the plan you marked for the Defence, which was D79. And do the same on that one for me, please, just sketch in your mother's house.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please mark on that map, as you would as an architect if drawing, her doorway.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've used a little arrow to indicate her doorway. Could you possibly write "doorway," D-O-O-R-W-A-Y, in English, on it.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: W and then --? I understand you well. Doesn't it -- there's an R and a W; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. W-A-Y.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you just leave that for one moment there. Can you please now turn to Exhibit D80. There is a photograph. I just want you to look at the photograph at the second page of D80. On the plan towards your left, I want you to orientate yourself as to the angle from where that photograph is taken, and I want you to draw an arrow with a little circle from the spot from where it's taken. Not on that building. Not on that one, but on the plan you've just marked. Could you just write above that circle "photo," P-H-O-T-O.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the end of the line, which is on the right, you've drawn a trajectory with a left and a right line. The left, is that the church, and the right, is that the building which is shown in the photo, marked as Buniceva Poljana 6?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is the building which you can see in the photograph? That's the one which is on the right, with the three storeys. Can you please hatch that in with crosses.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Can you just please put your name -- write your name down at the bottom of that exhibit on that page and just put a date on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 7th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be received into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document is P177.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please turn to -- in P174, two entries: X-3 and X-4.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've looked at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps the witness could just have back P177 for a moment, and please turn to the next one, which is X-4, and that describes a fountain. Can you just please mark on P177 where the fountain described in X-4 is. Can you maybe draw a circle around the actual fountain.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please just write underneath that, with an arrow, fountain, F-O-U-N-T-A-I-N.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vukovic. You were asked some questions about the times recorded in the report, the report you prepared, and you were asked about the fact that several described the same time of inspection of different buildings. What was the significance of recording the time of inspection as opposed to the date or the location or the damage in these particular forms?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it was decided to write in the time as well, but I think that for us this was not very relevant, and it wasn't really, for us, a very important reason to write it in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also described to Mr. Vukovic -- sorry, to Mr. Petrovic today about the difficult circumstances under which the report was compiled, namely, no electricity, water, et cetera. How were the photographs which were taken to accompany this report developed?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a fairly interesting question. Since there was no water, we developed it in the sea. That is why the photographs were mostly black and white, because at the time it was possible to develop them like that. But I don't understand why the Institute for the Protection of Cultural Monuments is not able to also use the same method to develop colour photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: While I'm asking the next question, can the witness please be shown Exhibit P172.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, Mr. Petrovic asked you about the Serbian Orthodox Church and damage to it, and you told him that you visited the priest in his apartment. Are you able to say, if you look at the P172, which is being brought to you, which is the list of maps, which apartment was his apartment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my learned colleague is interpreting incorrectly the evidence. The witness never said at any point in time that he had visited the priest. I don't remember him saying that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My recollection, or my note, says that he visited the priest in his apartment. That's my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Time, though, is the issue, the time at which it occurred, and I don't think there was evidence from him about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, when did you visit the priest to talk to him about the damage to the church? When was it in relation to the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was definitely after the 6th, and it was at the time that we were recording the damage in the building where his apartment is located. I think that is the Od Polaca Street. I don't know the exact number, but that was more or less the circumstance of the visit, but I don't know the time, because we did perhaps go to certain places two or three times, so I cannot tell you when this was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look in P172 are you able to tell us which is his apartment? If you look at the map of, say, block 9, 10, 11, or whichever? Are you able to give us the block number and the building number? That would be suitable for the purposes of this question.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is block 8, and that's somewhere in this row. So it could be here, there, or there. I think there are two entrances there, and that's somewhere in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All I want you to do: Could you turn to block 8 in that exhibit and just tell the Trial Chamber which of the buildings it was you think the priest -- you visited the priest in. If you flick through, you'll find a map which has an 8 marked on it, which corresponds to block 8.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm thinking now. It's 49, number 49.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, we only have a few minutes left. Are you able to say which one it is or not?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's this building here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... number 49?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Just a moment. [Interpretation] No. No. I'm mistaken. I think that it's this one, 44, right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated, for the purpose of the record, block 8, 44, and also putting your finger over possibly 41; is that correct? Meaning either one or other of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also asked about recording the names of --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN VUKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I made one mistake. It is difficult to identify the buildings based on this diagram, on this section of the diagram. I wish that I could have a larger diagram, where I could see a broader area. So then I could see it more clearly, and then I could explain why I made a mistake and instead of 44 I pointed to 49. But this is Od Polaca Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not pursuing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
